recolour.by_colour_map.definition: Output = input with a cellwise colour substitution phi (bijection or many-to-one) applied to every cell (optionally outside a key region, optionally after cropping to the main object); phi is either constant across pairs or read from in-grid legend pairs.

parameters.scope: whole grid | outside key | cropped main object

recolour.by_colour_map.detector: Same shape (or crop of largest object); for every cell, out colour is a function of in colour alone (consistent across all pairs, or consistent with legend adjacency pairs present in input).
recolour.by_colour_map.primitive_sketch:
phi = induce_map(pairs) or read_pairs(key_region(inp))
out = apply(phi, inp) on scope; if scope==crop: out = crop(largest_obj(out))

recolour.by_key_position.definition: Targets (objects, rows, columns, quadrants, rank-ordered segments) are recoloured with the colour of the key cell at the corresponding position of a small in-grid key (key column/row, minimap, corner cells, ordered legend stripes); key optionally erased and output optionally cropped to the target area.

parameters.key: region: first column/row, small multicolour block, corner cells, stripe list
parameters.correspondence: same row | same column | relative layout | rank order

recolour.by_key_position.detector: Input has a uniform target colour T and a small key K of distinct colours; every output T-cell colour equals K[pos(cell)] under one of the listed correspondences; non-T cells unchanged (or key erased/cropped away).

recolour.by_shape_match.definition: Each candidate object (uniform colour) whose shape equals an exemplar/key shape (up to translation, dihedral transform, optionally scale) is recoloured to that exemplar colour; unmatched candidates unchanged.

parameters.exemplars: shapes of distinct colours (in frames / corner / key)

recolour.by_shape_match.detector: Changed cells form whole candidate objects; each changed object shape-equals an input object of the new colour under the induced equivalence.

recolour.by_touching_marker.definition: Each target object/region/cell takes the colour of the marker associated with it (marker inside it, touching it, nearest to it, containing ancestor, or paired panel); markers optionally erased.

parameters.markers: singletons or lines of other colours
parameters.association: contains | 4/8-adjacent | nearest | enclosing ancestor | paired panel

recolour.by_touching_marker.detector: Every changed cell belongs to a target component whose new colour equals the colour of exactly one marker associated with it under one association rule; changes are constant per component.

recolour.object_by_property.definition: Each foreground object (component, row or panel) is recoloured by a table g(feature), feature from {size, size rank, shape/topology class, contains pattern, count of a colour, marker column}; objects not selected keep colour.
recolour.object_by_property.detector: Changes are constant per input object; new colour is a function of one computed object feature consistent over all pairs.
recolour.object_by_property.primitive_sketch:
objs = segment(inp, mode)
for f in FEATURES: g = induce_table(f, objs, pairs); if consistent: break
for o in objs: paint(o, g[f(o)]) if f(o) in g

recolour.by_ordinal_index.definition: Elements (columns, cells in scan order, objects, runs of rows, regions, cells along a line) are ordered along an axis; element with index i gets palette[i mod k] (or palette[i] for rank) where palette is induced.
recolour.by_ordinal_index.detector: Changed cells are exactly the fg cells of elements whose index mod k is in a fixed residue set (index counted from a consistent end); colour depends only on residue.

recolour.by_distance_layers.definition: Cell colour = palette[d mod k] (or palette[d]) where d is a distance of the cell from a source set (object boundary depth, seed cell, frame) under a metric (Chebyshev/Manhattan/geodesic in region); palette constant, from key, or reversed input layer colours.

parameters.palette: cycle constant | key sequence | reversed layers

recolour.by_distance_layers.detector: Within mask, output colour is a function of (d mod k) for one metric/source; cells outside mask unchanged.
recolour.by_distance_layers.primitive_sketch:
D = distance(mask, source, metric)
pal = induce(palette_source)
out[mask] = pal[D % len(pal)] (None = keep)

recolour.by_region_position.definition: Each container (object, panel, frame interior, lattice cell, whole grid) is split into position classes (halves, quadrants, 3x3 cells, border ring vs interior, corners vs edges); each class painted with a colour from a table (constant or from corner markers).
recolour.by_region_position.detector: Changed cells lie in containers; within a container the new colour depends only on the cell relative-position class.
recolour.by_region_position.primitive_sketch:
for C in containers(inp): for cell in C: cls = partition(C, cell)
  out[cell] = table[cls] (table induced or from markers at corners)

recolour.along_ray.definition: Straight lines are cast from source cells/objects (edge markers, odd block, endpoint pair) in induced directions; cells on the line are painted line colour and crossed objects/cells recoloured by rule (to line colour, bg, alt colour, or underlying region colour).
recolour.along_ray.detector: All changed cells lie on straight rows/cols/diagonals through source cells; change on each cell depends on its input colour class.
recolour.along_ray.primitive_sketch:
for s in sources: for dir in dirs: for cell on line(s,dir):
  out[cell] = rule(inp[cell], s.colour)  # rule table induced from pairs

recolour.template_sites.definition: Find every placement of a template (all-bg window of fixed shape, or a mixed-colour pattern with wildcards) and paint the union of placements (only its bg/target cells) with paint.

parameters.template: window shape (2x2, 3x3, plus) or learned motif

recolour.template_sites.detector: Changed cells = union of placements of one fixed shape where all covered input cells match the template.
recolour.template_sites.primitive_sketch:
T = induce_template(pairs); hits = [p for p in positions if matches(inp,T,p)]
for p in hits (greedy if overlap=nonoverlap): paint(target cells of T at p, paint)

fill.largest_empty.definition: Find the maximal empty (bg-only) shape of a family (axis rectangle, band, diagonal run) and paint it (optionally shrunk by 1).
fill.largest_empty.detector: Changed cells form one bg rectangle/segment of maximal size containing no fg.

recolour.cyclic_shift.definition: Colour-bearing regions are ordered cyclically (clockwise around core, along loop, left-to-right bands) and each takes the colour of its successor.

parameters.regions: sectors | boxes on loop | column bands

recolour.cyclic_shift.detector: Multiset of region colours preserved; each region new colour = old colour of a neighbour region in one consistent cyclic order.
recolour.cyclic_shift.primitive_sketch: R = ordered_regions(inp, order); for i: paint(R[i], colour(R[(i+s)%n]))

recolour.by_tiling.definition: Decompose a monochrome shape exactly into pieces from a fixed set (2x2 squares, bars, L-trominoes) and colour each piece by its type/orientation.
recolour.by_tiling.detector: Output partitions the input shape into pieces of the set, each piece monochrome with colour determined by its type.
recolour.by_tiling.primitive_sketch:
tiling = exact_cover(shape, pieces)  # backtracking
for p in tiling: paint(p.cells, table[p.type])

fill.bbox_bg.definition: For each object (component, cluster, or group of 4 corner markers, or cells of colour A), fill cells of target colour (default bg) inside its bbox (margin m, strict interior optional) with paint (constant or legend-mapped from object colour).

parameters.objects: components | corner groups | colour A cells

fill.bbox_bg.detector: Every changed cell lies in the bbox(+m) of some object and had target colour; all target cells in those bboxes changed.
fill.bbox_bg.primitive_sketch:
for o in group(inp, mode): B = bbox(o, margin)
  for c in B: if inp[c]==target: out[c]=paint_of(o)

fill.between_pair_on_line.definition: Per row and/or column, bg cells between two consecutive fg cells (optionally facing blocks, overlap span inset, only fully-bg spans, min span) are painted.
fill.between_pair_on_line.detector: Changed cells form horizontal/vertical runs of former bg whose two neighbours along the axis are endpoint-class cells.
fill.between_pair_on_line.primitive_sketch:
for line in lines(axis): for (a,b) consecutive endpoints on line:
  if cond(a,b): paint(cells strictly between a,b (inset), paint)

fill.region_by_property.definition: Segment bg into regions separated by walls; paint each region by a rule on a region feature: enclosed vs border-touching, area rank, rectangularity, size parity, colour of seed inside/adjacent, majority marker colour inside/on boundary.

parameters.feature: enclosed | area rank | is_rect | parity | seed colour | majority marker

fill.region_by_property.detector: Changed cells are whole bg components (under the walls); each component uniformly painted with a colour determined by one component feature.

combine.boolean_panels.definition: Split into two panels (halves, separator, or grid vs its mirror); output cell colour = truth table T(a_fg, b_fg) over the two fg masks, colours induced.
combine.boolean_panels.detector: Output shape equals a panel; output colour at each cell is a function of the fg bits of the corresponding panel cells.
combine.boolean_panels.primitive_sketch:
A,B = split(inp); T = induce_table(pairs)
out[c] = T[(A[c]!=bg, B[c]!=bg)]

combine.priority_overlay.definition: Split into k equal panels / overlapping windows; output cell = the non-bg value of highest priority (priority by colour order or panel order, induced).
combine.priority_overlay.detector: Output shape equals a panel; each output cell equals one of the corresponding panel cells, always the one ranked first by a fixed order.
combine.priority_overlay.primitive_sketch:
P = split(inp); order = induce_priority(pairs)
out[c] = min((v for v in [p[c] for p in P] if v!=bg), key=order, default=bg)

ca.local_rule.definition: Output cell = f(input neighbourhood of radius r), f a learned lookup (e.g. bg with diagonal fg neighbour -> paint, convex/concave loop corner -> colour); optionally applied after tiling.
ca.local_rule.detector: Output(c) is determined by the input window around c consistently across all pairs (no conflicting windows).
ca.local_rule.primitive_sketch:
g = pre(inp); table = {window(g,c,r): out[c]} from pairs
out[c] = table.get(window(g,c,r), g[c])

ca.row_recurrence.definition: Starting from seed rows, each subsequent row (step s) is computed from the previous row(s) by a local rule over diagonal/vertical neighbours; colours optionally alternate by level.
ca.row_recurrence.detector: For rows below the seed, out row r is a function of out row r-s cells (r-s, c-1..c+1).
ca.row_recurrence.primitive_sketch: for r from seed_end: out[r][c] = f(out[r-s][c-1], out[r-s][c], out[r-s][c+1], level parity)

ray.bounce.definition: A ray/path starts at a seed and travels diagonally or in zigzag, reflecting off grid edges or mirror-colour lines, passing through passable lines, until exiting.
ray.bounce.detector: Changed cells form a diagonal path whose direction flips only at edges or reflector cells.
ray.bounce.primitive_sketch:
p,d = seed; while in_grid(p): paint(p); if blocked(p+d): d = reflect(d)
 p += d

stamp.reflect_recoloured.definition: Reflect an object across an axis (separator line, object edge marked by markers, or towards a marker dot) and paint the copy (and/or original) with a recolouring induced from markers.
stamp.reflect_recoloured.detector: Output = input plus a mirrored copy of an object about an axis adjacent to it; copy colours are a colour map of the original.
stamp.reflect_recoloured.primitive_sketch:
axis = find_axis(inp); copy = reflect(obj, axis)
paint(copy, phi(obj colours)); optionally recolour original

move.translate_recolour.definition: All foreground translated by a constant vector and recoloured by a colour map.
move.translate_recolour.detector: Output fg equals shifted input fg with uniform colour change.
move.translate_recolour.primitive_sketch: out = apply(phi, shift(inp, v)); v, phi induced

summarise.class_to_constant.definition: Classify the input (dominant colour, binary shape mask) and output a fixed glyph from a table indexed by the class.
summarise.class_to_constant.detector: Outputs are constant for inputs with the same class; output size constant.
summarise.class_to_constant.primitive_sketch: k = classify(inp); return TABLE[k]  # TABLE induced from train

segment.filter_objects.definition: Delete objects failing a predicate on a count of a marker colour inside them (e.g. keep count<=1, remove argmin).
segment.filter_objects.detector: Output = input with some whole components erased; erased set determined by marker counts.
segment.filter_objects.primitive_sketch:
objs = components(inp); n = count(o, marker)
erase(o for o in objs if not pred(n(o), all n))

segment.pack_pieces.definition: Translate (and possibly rotate) the pieces so that they tile a fixed-size rectangle/frame exactly.
segment.pack_pieces.detector: Output cells counts per colour equal input piece cell counts; output is a filled rectangle.
segment.pack_pieces.primitive_sketch: for placement of pieces (backtracking): if exact cover of target: return

stamp.template_at_markers.definition: One multi-cell template object exists in the input; every marker (lone cell or small cluster not part of the template) receives a translated copy of the template, positioned by an anchor rule; the copy may be recoloured to the marker colour or transformed by a per-anchor-colour dihedral; original template/markers optionally erased; output may be the grid or the concatenation of copies.

parameters.markers: singleton cells (or tiny clusters) of marker colour(s)
parameters.anchor_rule: centre | same-colour cell of template | fixed offset | sequence index
parameters.transform: identity | dihedral keyed by anchor colour

stamp.template_at_markers.detector: Input has exactly one object with >=3 cells (template) and >=1 marker singletons; each output diff region is congruent (up to recolour/dihedral) to the template and contains/centres on a marker cell with consistent relative offset across all markers and pairs.

stamp.complete_partial_matches.definition: A complete reference template (a multicolour object, or a patch plus its frame) is present; every other object/configuration that equals a subset of the template under an allowed transform group G (dihedral) and scale s is completed by painting the missing template cells in place (colours from template, or a fixed paint colour).

parameters.template: most complete object / object containing the frame colour
parameters.match_domain: objects | windows in noise | lattice cells

stamp.complete_partial_matches.detector: Output ⊇ input; every added cell set, together with an input fragment, forms a copy of one template (under some g∈G, scale s); every fragment is a proper subset of that copy with >=1 cell of distinctive colour.
stamp.complete_partial_matches.primitive_sketch:
T=select_templates(I)  # completest
for frag in candidates(I, domain): for g,s in G×S: if frag ⊆ place(g(scale(T,s)),at): paint missing
params G,S,domain,paint chosen as smallest set consistent with all train pairs

stamp.copy_to_congruent_target.definition: A source object carries a pattern; target regions have the same outline/size as the source (silhouette of placeholder colour, same-colour plain rect, same-size frame, or empty bg hole) and receive the source pattern (optionally mirrored, 9-slice resized, or recoloured to the target frame colour); unmatched targets or the source may be erased.

parameters.target_key: silhouette colour | frame colour+size | bg hole of source interior size

stamp.copy_to_congruent_target.detector: Each changed output region coincides with an input region whose shape (bbox or cell mask) equals the source's shape/interior; the output content there equals T(source pattern) for one T across all pairs.

stamp.panel_copy.definition: Grid is partitioned into panels by separator lines; the content of the source panel(s) is copied into target panels chosen by a rule (all, marked, same frame colour, parity lattice, pattern continuation) with an optional per-target transform (rotation by index) or recolour (separator colour).

parameters.targets: all | marked | same frame colour | same parity | continuation

stamp.panel_copy.detector: Separator lines partition input into equal panels; every changed panel in output equals T(source panel) for a single source panel; unchanged panels keep input.

stamp.local_stencil.definition: Each seed (single cell, 2x2 block, or small object matched by a local pattern) gets a fixed relative stencil of cells painted around it; stencil offsets/colours are a function of the seed's colour (or taken from the seed's own cells), optionally gated by context (inside region, nearest border colour) and optionally erasing the seed.

parameters.stencil: map offset→colour (constant, seed colour, or seed-part colour)
parameters.gate: none | inside region colour | nearest border line

stamp.local_stencil.detector: All diff cells lie within Chebyshev radius r (<=2) of seeds; grouping diffs by seed gives the same (offset→colour) map for all seeds with same colour signature across all train pairs.
stamp.local_stencil.primitive_sketch:
seeds=find_seeds(I, pattern)
stencil[sig]=learn_offset_colour_map(train diffs grouped by seed signature)
for s in seeds if gate(s): paint(O, s.pos+off, colour(sig,s)) for off in stencil[sig]; erase if flagged

stamp.stencil_at_computed_point.definition: A fixed stencil (plus, 3x3 ring, cross of marker colours) is painted at a point computed from markers: midpoint of two markers, centroid of three markers, or intersection of a horizontal and vertical line.

parameters.markers: 2-3 singleton cells or two full lines

stamp.stencil_at_computed_point.detector: Diff cells form one fixed-shape stencil whose centre equals the midpoint/centroid/intersection of the non-bg input markers in every train pair.
stamp.stencil_at_computed_point.primitive_sketch:
pts=find_markers(I); c=point_rule(pts)  # try midpoint,centroid,intersection
paint(O, c+stencil, paint)

stamp.grow_ring.definition: Around each object (or seed) paint a metric ball/ring (Chebyshev square or Manhattan diamond) of thickness/radius r computed from an object property (inner-core size, count of inner dots, distance to nearest obstacle minus 1, half segment length), colour from a role, painting only background.

parameters.r: core size | dot count | dist-1 | len/2 | 1

stamp.grow_ring.detector: Output ⊇ input; all new cells for each object lie at metric distance 1..r from it (or its centre) and fill that shell completely except where blocked; r matches one property function across pairs.
stamp.grow_ring.primitive_sketch:
for o in objects(I): r=prop(o); shell=dilate(o or centre(o), r, metric)-o
paint_bg(O, shell, colour(o))

stamp.bbox_outline.definition: Draw a 1-cell rectangle outline defined by the bbox of selected cells (markers, all cells of a colour, or the whole grid), optionally inset/outset by d, in a paint colour; optionally erase everything else / the seed.

parameters.cells: marker colour | mode colour | whole grid

stamp.bbox_outline.detector: Output diff equals (outline of bbox(selected cells) shifted by d) painted in one colour, possibly plus erasure of non-outline cells.

stamp.count_bar.definition: Draw one straight bar per counted item whose length equals an induced count (cells per colour, distinct colours in a block, difference of two colour counts), placed at a slot relative to the item (next slot, below block, beside key entry, histogram column).
stamp.count_bar.detector: Every diff component is a 1-wide straight segment (or width = item width) whose length equals a count computed from the input; segments ordered/placed by items.
stamp.count_bar.primitive_sketch: for it in items(I): n=count_fn(it); draw_bar(O, anchor(it), dir, n, colour(it))

stamp.residual.definition: Tasks whose STAMP step is embedded in a task-specific pipeline (rays, moves, summaries) or uses a bespoke template.

residual_reasons.9772c176: triangle caps on flat sides, bespoke
residual_reasons.ecdecbb3: ray then frame stamp at contact
residual_reasons.a2d730bd: connect stray to rect with bump
residual_reasons.ac3e2b04: ray through anchors + ring at intersections
residual_reasons.673ef223: ray from bar to dots + copy to other bar (RAY)
residual_reasons.695367ec: grid lines period N+1 on fixed canvas

tile.block_placement.definition: Output is a block lattice of input-sized (or template-sized) blocks; block (i,j) holds template X (input, colour-swapped input, fixed 2x2 checker, downscaled template) iff mask(i,j), where mask = X==fg, X==bg, uniform row/col index, or first k blocks in reading order (k=count).

parameters.mask: X==fg | X==bg | uniform line index | first k (k=fg count)

tile.block_placement.detector: Output dims are integer multiples of a block size; every block is either all-bg or equal to one fixed block X; the set of filled blocks matches one mask rule.
tile.block_placement.primitive_sketch:
X=template_rule(I); M=mask_rule(I)
O=zeros(M.h*X.h, M.w*X.w); for (i,j) where M: O[block i,j]=X

tile.arrangement.definition: Output = fixed arrangement of transformed copies of the input (or its cropped object): n×m repeat, rotations around centre, frame+stack; then an optional learned local post-rule (stencil/column projection) applied on the tiled canvas.

parameters.layout: n x m | 4 rotations around centre | vertical stack with shared border

tile.arrangement.detector: Output dims = k·input dims (+border); after undoing post-rule cells, each slot equals a dihedral image of the input.
tile.arrangement.primitive_sketch:
C=assemble([g_s(X) for slot s in layout])
return post_rule(C)  # post learned from diff of assemble vs output

residual_reasons.d304284e: tile to edge with every-3rd recolour

complete.symmetry_global.definition: Whole grid (or the single motif around a centre anchor/separator axes) is symmetric under an inferred group (mirror H/V, rot90, rot180, D4) about an inferred centre; missing or occluder-coloured cells are filled from their orbit (optionally in a paint colour).

parameters.group: H | V | HV | rot90 | rot180 | D4
parameters.centre: grid centre | anchor | separator lines | offset search

complete.symmetry_global.detector: There exist group G and centre c such that all non-masked input cells are consistent with G-orbits; output = orbit fill of masked cells.
complete.symmetry_global.primitive_sketch:
G,c=search_symmetry(I, mask)  # maximise consistency
for cell in masked: O[cell]=paint or vote(I[orbit(cell)])

complete.symmetry_per_object.definition: Same as symmetry_global but applied independently inside each object/frame: axis from an in-object line, frame notches, or best-fit; noise outside frames/occluder erased.
complete.symmetry_per_object.detector: Per object/frame, output content is mirror-symmetric about an axis detectable from the input and ⊇ input content (minus occluder/noise).
complete.symmetry_per_object.primitive_sketch: for R in scopes(I): ax=axis(R); R[:]=union(R, mirror(R,ax)); erase(noise)

complete.period.definition: Grid (or lattice of sites) follows a 2D period (possibly diagonal); cells masked by holes/occluders or missing lattice sites are restored from the period (missing sites optionally painted a new colour or marked).
complete.period.detector: Minimal period P fits all unmasked cells; output = periodic extension over masked cells.
complete.period.primitive_sketch:
P=min_period(I, ignore=mask)
for cell in mask: O[cell]=paint if newsite else I[canon(cell,P)]

complete.prefix_by_template.definition: Rows/bands are prefixes of a full template row/band; each prefix is extended to full length following the template (through a colour map induced from the prefix, or in a new paint colour).

parameters.colour: colour map from prefix | new paint

complete.prefix_by_template.detector: One row/band is full; every other non-empty row/band equals the template's prefix under a colour bijection; output extends them.
complete.prefix_by_template.primitive_sketch: T=full_row(I); for r in partial_rows: m=bijection(T[:len], r); O[r]=paint_new or m(T)

complete.rectangle.definition: Objects are solid (possibly overlapping) rectangles corrupted by a noise colour; restore each rectangle and erase noise.
complete.rectangle.detector: Output components are all axis-aligned solid rectangles whose union covers input rectangle-colour cells.
complete.rectangle.primitive_sketch: for c in colours-noise: R=bbox(c); fill R; noise→bg

complete.residual.definition: Constraint-style or bespoke completions (latin square, colour-set, panel merge, move+occlusion, dashed-line gaps).

residual_reasons.c6e1b8da: move by tail + occluded rect completion
residual_reasons.4612dd53: fill gaps in lines of rectangle skeleton

move.slide_until_contact.definition: Every mover object (connected component, rigid) is translated along one axis direction until it touches a non-background cell or the grid edge; direction is a global constant or a lookup keyed by an object property (colour, shape class, containing region). Movers processed nearest-to-destination first so they stack. Optional: paint swept cells, recolour by class.

parameters.mover_selector: colour / shape predicate (e.g. contains 2x2, ring vs cross)

move.slide_until_contact.detector: Output objects of mover colour are congruent to input objects and displaced along a single axis; after displacement each touches the edge or a non-mover cell in the direction of travel; all non-mover cells unchanged.
move.slide_until_contact.primitive_sketch:
dir_of = induce map from {const, colour, class, region} that explains train
for obj in sorted(movers, key=dist_to_edge(dir_of(obj))): erase(obj); shift obj by dir until next cell hits non-bg/edge; paint(obj); optionally paint swept cells trail_colour

move.toward_anchor.definition: Each mover (cell or object) moves straight toward the anchor it is paired with (same colour border/line/block, or nearest aligned anchor) until adjacent to it; unpaired/unaligned movers are erased or kept by an induced flag.

parameters.pairing: same colour | nearest aligned | compatibility table
parameters.unmatched: erase | keep | send to far edge

move.toward_anchor.detector: Every changed mover ends orthogonally/diagonally adjacent to (or stacked against) an anchor it was aligned with in the input and moved along the line joining them; anchors unchanged.
coverage_risk: d687bc17 (dot stops next to side, frame not an obstacle object)
move.toward_anchor.primitive_sketch:
anchors = select(anchor_selector); for m in movers: a = pair(m, anchors) (same colour / nearest aligned)
if a is None: apply unmatched policy; else dir = sign(a - m); slide m by dir until adjacent to a or blocked

move.by_vector.definition: Each object is translated by a vector computed from its own properties or a global count: v = k * unit_dir where k in {1, width, height, size, marker count} or v = map(colour).

parameters.unit_dir: dir8 constant | toward anchor | toward marked corner | away from floor
parameters.magnitude: 1 | own width | own height | cell count | count(markers) | map(colour)

move.by_vector.detector: Output objects are congruent translates of input objects; for every object the displacement equals a fixed function of that object (size, bbox dim, colour) consistent across all train pairs.
move.by_vector.primitive_sketch:
for obj: feats = {w,h,size,colour,count_markers}; induce v(obj) = dir(obj)*f(feats) from train by search over small feature set
erase all; paint obj at pos+v (clip)

move.to_position.definition: Mover is placed so a reference point of it (a key-coloured cell, centre, corner) coincides with a target point defined by an anchor (matching-colour marker cell, lattice-cell centre, opposite frame corner, anchor-block cell in same quadrant); original erased.

parameters.target: matching colour marker | lattice cell centre | reflected corner of frame | quadrant anchor cell

move.to_position.detector: Each output mover is a translate (optionally dihedral image) of an input object whose reference cell lands exactly on a cell defined by an anchor that exists in the input; source cells cleared.
move.to_position.primitive_sketch:
pairs = match(movers, targets by colour/quadrant/cell)
for m,t in pairs: T = argmin dihedral s.t. ref colours align (identity default); erase m; paint T(m) translated so ref(m)->t

move.fit_into_hole.definition: Loose pieces are matched to holes/cavities/gaps/complementary profiles of container objects by shape (optionally rotation) and translated so they exactly fill it; unmatched pieces/noise erased.

parameters.container_selector: objects with holes / floor with gaps / profiles
parameters.match: exact shape | up to rotation | complement profile

move.fit_into_hole.detector: For each moved piece there is an input container whose background hole has the same shape as the piece (mod rotation); in output the hole is filled with piece colour and piece's old cells are bg.
move.fit_into_hole.primitive_sketch:
holes = bg components enclosed/indented by containers; for piece in pieces: h = find hole with shape(piece)==shape(h) (try rot)
erase piece; paint piece colour on h; erase unmatched/noise

transform.kronecker.definition: Fractal/Kronecker product: output is an (H*h)x(W*w) grid of blocks; block (i,j) = tile_on(in[i,j]) if pred(in[i,j]) else tile_off, where tile_on is the input itself, the input masked to colour c, or a legend motif for c.

parameters.tile_on: input | mask(input==c) painted c | legend motif(c) | panel

transform.kronecker.detector: Output dims are product of input dims (or of mask and tile dims); each output block equals either a fixed tile or empty, and the on/off pattern equals a predicate on the corresponding input cell.
transform.kronecker.primitive_sketch:
mask_src,tile_src = induce roles; for (i,j) in mask: block = tile_on(mask[i,j]) if pred(mask[i,j]) else tile_off
out = assemble blocks; pred from {==C, most frequent, least frequent, !=bg}

transform.tile_dihedral.definition: Output is an r x c arrangement of dihedral images of a source S (whole input, cropped object, recoloured input, quadrant), possibly with shared-edge overlap; r,c constant or from a count (distinct colours, markers, input side).

parameters.source: whole | fg bbox crop | quadrant | colour-swapped
parameters.layout: r x c matrix of dihedral ops

transform.tile_dihedral.detector: Output size is a multiple (minus overlaps) of source size and every output block equals one of the 8 dihedral images of the same source.
transform.tile_dihedral.primitive_sketch:
S = source(in); (r,c) = count(in); ops = induce per-block dihedral from train output blocks
out = concat_grid([[ops[i][j](S) for j] for i], overlap)

transform.scale.definition: Output is the source (whole input, fg bbox, inner block, sampled lattice) upscaled by an integer factor k (constant, #distinct colours) or to fit a target frame interior; optional non-uniform per-row/col factors.

parameters.source: whole | fg crop | inner block | sampled lattice

transform.scale.detector: Output = source with every cell replaced by a k x k (or kr x kc) block; checkable by downsampling output.
transform.scale.primitive_sketch:
S = source(in); k = induce from {const, n_colours, target_dim/src_dim}
out = repeat(repeat(S,k,axis0),k,axis1); if frame: place in frame interior

transform.dihedral.definition: Output = one dihedral op D applied to a source (whole grid, crop, block-summary, tile-lattice of motifs); D constant or inferred from an in-grid example pair or marker layout.

parameters.source: whole | crop | block summary | lattice of motif tiles
parameters.D: const | inferred from example pair | chosen to match markers

transform.dihedral.detector: Some D in the dihedral group maps source to output exactly (at cell or tile granularity).
transform.dihedral.primitive_sketch:
S = source(in) at granularity g; D = const from train or argmin_D match(D(A),B) / marker layout
out = D(S) (tiles moved as units when g=tile)

transform.row_shift.definition: Each row (or column) is shifted horizontally by s(r): linear shear relative to an anchor row, periodic sequence, parity, or a constant roll given by a marker offset; cyclic (roll) or with padding/clamp.

parameters.mode: cyclic | pad bg | clamp to object

transform.row_shift.detector: For every row r, out row r equals in row r shifted by an integer s(r); s fits one of the listed families.
coverage_risk: 025d127b (bottom row fixed, clamp at max column)
transform.row_shift.primitive_sketch:
for each r: find s(r) in train by matching rows; fit family (linear/periodic/const-from-marker)
out[r] = shift(in[r], s(r), mode)

transform.reflect_object.definition: An object is reflected across an axis given by a marker/bracket/line/bbox edge (or its own centre); copy is OR-ed with original or replaces it, optionally painted in marker colour.

parameters.axis: bbox edge facing marker | bracket | explicit line | centre object | own centre

transform.reflect_object.detector: Output new cells = reflection of an input object across a line determined by input geometry; with keep_original false the source cells become bg.
coverage_risk: f8a8fe49 (split at centre, halves reflected separately)
transform.reflect_object.primitive_sketch:
for obj: axis = induce(axis_source); cp = reflect(obj, axis)
if not keep_original: erase(obj); paint(cp, paint_colour)

transform.rotate_about_pivot.definition: A segment/offset is rotated by 90 degrees about a pivot cell (anchor, marked pivot, bar base) and repainted; source erased.

parameters.pivot: anchor cell | marked cell | bar base

transform.rotate_about_pivot.detector: Changed cells are the 90-degree rotation of removed cells about a single pivot cell per object.
transform.rotate_about_pivot.primitive_sketch: for each (pivot, part): rot = rotate_offsets(part - pivot, angle); erase part; paint pivot + rot

extend.periodic_fill.definition: A periodic pattern (1D or 2D, possibly diagonal-shifted translation lattice) visible in a known region is continued over the whole canvas (possibly enlarged), overwriting noise/strip/bg cells.

parameters.known_region: non-bg cells | outside noise strip | per bg-region

extend.periodic_fill.detector: There exist translations such that the output is invariant under them and output agrees with input on the known-region cells.
extend.periodic_fill.primitive_sketch:
known = mask(in); for (py,px,shift) in small search: if consistent(known): break
out = canvas; out[y,x] = representative of lattice class of (y,x)

extend.periodic_lines.definition: Full lines are drawn perpendicular to an axis at positions seed + k*p (p from seed spacing), colours cycling through seed colours/legend; optional caps.
extend.periodic_lines.detector: Output contains full rows/cols of seed colours at arithmetic positions, colour sequence periodic.
coverage_risk: e7b06bea (run length k from corner marker)
extend.periodic_lines.primitive_sketch:
seeds = sorted seed cells; p = spacing; cols = cycle(seed colours)
for k: draw full line at seed0 + k*p in cols[k]; add caps

extend.repeat_stamp.definition: A template object is copied repeatedly along a translation vector (from marker/fragment/object dims) until edge or target, each copy optionally recoloured.
extend.repeat_stamp.detector: Output new cells are translates of one input object by multiples of a fixed vector.
extend.repeat_stamp.primitive_sketch:
t = template; v = induce vector from marker/fragment
k=1..: paint(t shifted k*v, colour_k) until out of grid/stop

extend.sequence_positions.definition: Seed items (cells/rings) are repeated at positions following an arithmetic/triangular sequence inferred from seeds, colours cycling.
extend.sequence_positions.detector: New cells lie on the seed line at positions continuing the seed position sequence.
extend.sequence_positions.primitive_sketch:
pos = seed positions; fit gaps d_i (const or +1)
continue positions until edge; paint colours cycling (or constant)

extend.staircase.definition: From a seed bar, successive parallel bars at distance k have length L0 + a*k (a per side), colour per side or by parity.

parameters.range: until length 0 / grid edge / W/2 rows

extend.staircase.detector: Output bars parallel to seed with lengths an arithmetic progression of distance.
extend.staircase.primitive_sketch: seed = bar; for side in sides: for k=1..: L = L0 + delta[side]*k; if L<=0 break; draw bar at offset k colour[side/parity]

extend.stretch_to_marker.definition: A framed rectangle is stretched along an axis until it reaches a marker singleton; marker erased, internal structure (frame/dividers) preserved.
extend.stretch_to_marker.detector: Output rectangle = input rectangle with one side moved to marker's row/column; interior pattern extended.
extend.stretch_to_marker.primitive_sketch: for m in markers: side = side of rect facing m; extend side to m row/col; redraw frame+interior

extend.smear.definition: Each coloured cell in a key line is smeared parallel to a bar / upward until next colour or span end.
extend.smear.detector: Changed cells copy colour of nearest seed along direction.
extend.smear.primitive_sketch: for seed in key cells: walk direction painting seed colour until stop

ray.full_line.definition: Each seed (singleton cell, or a designated cell/axis of an object such as a domino's orientation or a block's centre) paints its entire row and/or column (axis chosen per seed colour or object orientation), optionally clipped to an enclosing region (band, cropped rectangle). Crossings resolved by a priority order or painted with a new constant colour; original objects stay on top.

parameters.seed: singleton cells | object centre | object long axis

ray.full_line.detector: Output same size (or = crop of region); every changed cell lies on a full row/col (or full span of the clipping region) that passes through a seed; per-colour axis table consistent across pairs.

ray.orthogonal_directed.definition: Each seed cell/object emits an axis-aligned half-ray in a direction given by a rule (fixed per colour, toward/away from an aligned target, toward the nearest edge, pointing out of the object away from its odd cell) and stops at the edge, just before the first non-bg cell, or at contact with the target. Paint = seed colour or role colour, optionally a periodic pattern.

parameters.seed: singleton cells | odd cell / apex of object | object rows/cols
parameters.dir_rule: colour->dir | toward aligned target | away from separator | nearest edge(s) | away from odd cell
parameters.stop: edge | before obstacle | adjacent to target
parameters.blockers: colour class that stops the ray

ray.orthogonal_directed.detector: Every added cell lies on a straight axis-aligned run starting at a seed and ending at the border or next to a non-bg cell; each run has constant colour equal to seed colour (or a constant); direction consistent with a learned rule across pairs.
ray.orthogonal_directed.primitive_sketch:
for s in seeds: for dir in dir_rule(s): walk from s in dir painting paint(s) until stop(cell)
induce dir_rule by testing candidate rules on train; stop by testing {edge, before-nonbg, adj-target}

ray.diagonal_from_object.definition: Diagonal rays emitted from selected corners of objects (all corners, the missing corner of an L-triomino, closed-side corners of a cup, marker-flagged corners, or a single seed's 4 diagonals) outward to the border or until non-bg, in object/role colour, optionally with beam width = object width and after a canvas rescale.

parameters.corner_sel: all | missing | closed-side | flagged | by colour->direction

ray.diagonal_from_object.detector: All added cells lie on 45-degree lines starting at a corner cell of an input object (after optional scaling); per line constant colour.
ray.diagonal_from_object.primitive_sketch:
g=pre(inp); objs=segment(g)
for o in objs: for (c,dir) in corner_sel(o): cast diagonal from c+dir, width w, colour paint(o), until stop
induce corner_sel/paint by enumerating rules consistent with train

ray.periodic_motif.definition: A seed emits a trail along a direction in which a fixed short motif (separator/own colour alternation, 2-step staircase, dotted stride) is repeated to the border.
ray.periodic_motif.detector: Added cells form a periodic sequence along a line/diagonal from each seed to the border; period and motif identical across pairs.
ray.periodic_motif.primitive_sketch:
for s in seeds: for dir in dirs: k=1; while inside: stamp motif[k%p] at s+k*dir; k+=1
learn motif and dirs from diff of first train pair

ray.walker_turn_split.definition: A ray from a seed (usually on an edge) travels straight; on hitting an obstacle it reacts by a policy: split perpendicular both ways, turn cw/ccw keyed by obstacle colour, reflect off a wall, or spiral; continues until edge. Paint = seed colour or constant.
ray.walker_turn_split.detector: Added cells form a single polyline/tree of axis/diagonal runs from a seed; each bend occurs adjacent to an obstacle cell.
ray.walker_turn_split.primitive_sketch:
queue=[(seed,dir0)]; while queue: pos,dir=pop; step; if blocked: push per policy(dir,obstacle colour)
paint visited; induce policy by trying the finite set on train

path.walker_detour.definition: Rays from seeds advance in a fixed direction; when the next cell is an obstacle they sidestep (fixed side or nearest free) around it and resume the original direction, ending at the border.

parameters.sidestep: right | left | nearest free | around bbox

path.walker_detour.detector: Each added path is monotone in the main direction, deviates only beside obstacles, and returns to its column/row after passing.
path.walker_detour.primitive_sketch:
for s in seeds: p=s; while inside: if free(p+dir): p+=dir else p=sidestep(p); paint p
learn sidestep rule from train

ray.container_leak.definition: Hollow container/bracket objects with an opening: interior is filled with a paint colour and a beam of the same colour escapes through the opening (width = opening, optional diagonal flare) to the edge.
ray.container_leak.detector: Added cells = container interior plus straight beam(s) starting at gap cells and running outward to the border.
ray.container_leak.primitive_sketch: for c in hollow(objs): fill interior(c); for gap g of c: cast beam outward (width |g|) ; optionally diagonals from gap ends

select.empty_lines_paint.definition: Rows/columns that contain no foreground (globally, or within the span of an object / block lattice) are painted with a constant colour (optionally different colours inside vs outside the fg bbox).
select.empty_lines_paint.detector: Changed cells are exactly bg cells on lines that are entirely bg (inside the relevant span); single new colour (or two by inside/outside bbox).
select.empty_lines_paint.primitive_sketch:
lines=[r for r in rows+cols if all bg in scope(r)]
paint lines (full length) with paint_in inside fg bbox, paint_out outside

project.and_intersection.definition: Markers along a border row and border column (or colour runs of a legend row/column) project across the grid; a cell is painted where a row-projection and column-projection intersect (AND), with the marker colour or a constant, optionally only inside a target rectangle.
project.and_intersection.detector: Every changed cell (r,c) has a marker in row r on the side edge and a marker in column c on the top/bottom edge (same colour if colour-keyed).
project.and_intersection.primitive_sketch:
R={r:col of marker in edge col}; C={c: colour of marker in edge row}
for r in R for c in C: if region(r,c) and key match: paint

project.marker_onto_target.definition: A marker cell is transported along its row/col to a landing position (first cell of target object, cell adjacent to a separator, far edge cell) and only the landing cell is painted (source kept or erased).

parameters.marker: cells on border / scattered fg / object axis
parameters.landing: first target cell | adjacent to stop | far edge

project.marker_onto_target.detector: Output differs from input only at landing cells (and optionally erased sources); each landing cell is aligned with exactly one source marker.
project.marker_onto_target.primitive_sketch: for m in markers: p=walk(m,dir) until landing rule; paint p; if not keep_source: erase m

connect.aligned_pair.definition: Pairs of same-colour cells/objects aligned on a row, column or diagonal (nearest facing partner) are joined by a straight segment between their facing tips, painted with a constant or the pair colour.

parameters.half_colour: optional split halves by endpoint colour + midpoint colour

connect.aligned_pair.detector: Every added cell lies strictly between two aligned same-class items on a straight line with no other fg between them.
connect.aligned_pair.primitive_sketch:
for a,b in pairs(items) if aligned(a,b) and clear_between: draw segment(facing tips) with paint
induce align set and paint from train

connect.lattice_between.definition: Grid partitioned into a lattice of tiles; tiles with the same mark (colour at same intra-tile position, or matching an exemplar) in the same lattice row/col cause the tiles/gaps between them to be filled with that mark (or new colour; overlap -> mix colour).
connect.lattice_between.detector: Output = input except tiles lying between two same-marked tiles in one lattice row/col, which receive the mark.
connect.lattice_between.primitive_sketch:
L=lattice(inp); for each lattice row/col: for same-mark pairs (i<j): mark tiles i..j
apply connect on the coarse tile grid then upsample

path.elbow_route.definition: Draw a route between 2-3 marker cells using a fixed move order (vertical-then-horizontal, horizontal-then-vertical, diagonal-then-straight, king moves), chained across markers; paint new constant or marker colour on bg only.
path.elbow_route.detector: Added cells form an elbow/octilinear polyline whose endpoints are adjacent to/at markers; one bend.
path.elbow_route.primitive_sketch:
for (a,b) in chain(endpoints): for leg in move_order: advance from a toward b along leg axis painting bg
induce move_order by fitting train

path.shortest_route.definition: Endpoints (same-colour cells/segments) are joined by a shortest 4-connected path avoiding obstacle cells (or crossing barriers only at their gaps).
path.shortest_route.detector: Added cells form a connected path between endpoints whose length equals BFS distance avoiding obstacles.
path.shortest_route.primitive_sketch: for group in endpoint sets: path=bfs(a,b, passable=bg|gap); paint path (tie-break learned)

crop.odd_one_out.definition: Segment panels/objects; output the one whose content differs from all others (unique pattern, unique colour, unique (a)symmetry).
crop.odd_one_out.detector: Output equals exactly one input unit (bbox crop) and that unit is the unique one w.r.t. some feature in each pair.
crop.odd_one_out.primitive_sketch: units=segment(inp); for f in features: u=[x for x in units if count(f(x)) == 1]; if len(u)==1: return crop(u)

crop.by_score.definition: Segment objects/frames; select the one maximising/minimising a score (count of marker colour/sub-pattern, size, adjacency to marker, inclusion in guides, content colour = frame colour) and output its bbox or interior.
crop.by_score.detector: Output equals the crop (bbox or interior) of one input unit that is the arg-extremum of a score in every train pair.
crop.by_score.primitive_sketch: units=segment(inp); for score in library: pick=argext(units,score); if all train match crop(pick,part): use it

crop.canonical_window.definition: Output is a window of the input chosen canonically: a fixed corner window, the top-left quadrant of a symmetric object's bbox (fundamental domain), or one period of a periodic grid.

parameters.window: fixed corner+size | quadrant of bbox | one period along axis

crop.canonical_window.detector: Output equals a subgrid of input located at a fixed/derived position; or input is periodic/symmetric and output is one fundamental tile.
crop.canonical_window.primitive_sketch: cands=[fixed windows, bbox quadrants, minimal period tile]; return first candidate matching all train

crop.overlay_windows.definition: Several equal-size windows/fragments (aligned by frame or by a shared anchor cell) are overlaid with non-base cells winning, output = the overlay.

parameters.windows: equal framed panels | fragments with anchor colour

crop.overlay_windows.detector: All windows same size after alignment; every output cell equals the non-base value in some window at that position.
crop.overlay_windows.primitive_sketch: W=segment windows; align; out=base; for w in W: out[w!=base]=w

crop.fit_by_anchor.definition: Pieces carrying a marker cell/constellation are translated so that their markers coincide with matching markers in a target panel/canvas; output = the target region.
crop.fit_by_anchor.detector: Output size = target region; each piece appears in output translated (no rotation) so its markers land on same-colour target markers.
crop.fit_by_anchor.primitive_sketch: T=target region; for p in pieces: find t so markers(p)+t == markers(T) subset; stamp p at t; return crop(T)

crop.fit_by_shape.definition: Host region with holes; each loose piece whose shape (up to dihedral) matches a hole is inserted into it; output = the host bbox.
crop.fit_by_shape.detector: Output = host bbox where each hole is replaced by a piece of identical (dihedral) shape from elsewhere in input.
crop.fit_by_shape.primitive_sketch: H=host; for hole in holes(H): p=match(pieces,shape(hole),dihedral); paint p into hole; return crop(H)

crop.extract_and_concat.definition: Selected pieces (objects passing a predicate, or strips between paired markers, or panel shapes) are each cropped and concatenated in positional order along the axis of spread (or packed in a 2x2 layout preserving quadrant).

parameters.pieces: objects | strips between markers | panel contents

crop.extract_and_concat.detector: Output is a concatenation of subgrids each equal to (possibly recoloured) crops from input, ordered by input position.
crop.extract_and_concat.primitive_sketch:
P=sorted([crop(p) for p in pieces if filter(p)], key=pos along axis)
return concat(P, axis) or grid2x2(P)

complete.crop_occluded.definition: Input is a symmetric/periodic pattern with a solid occluder rectangle; the occluded content is reconstructed and only the occluder region is output.
complete.crop_occluded.detector: Output size = occluder rect size; output cells equal pattern values predicted by symmetry/period.
complete.crop_occluded.primitive_sketch: M=occluder bbox; G=complete(inp, model, mask=M); return G[M]

summarise.panel_to_pixel.definition: Grid is split into panels (by separator lines, equal kxk blocks, or solid rectangles in a row/col layout); output has one pixel per panel given by a reduction (majority colour, single non-bg colour, bg colour, predicate->colour).

parameters.partition: separator lines | equal blocks | component layout

summarise.panel_to_pixel.detector: Output dims = panel layout dims; each output pixel is a function of the corresponding panel only.
summarise.panel_to_pixel.primitive_sketch: P=partition(inp) (grid of panels); out[i][j]=reduce(P[i][j]); induce reduce from library

summarise.count_to_glyph.definition: Count N of a selected item class (cells, objects, 2x2 squares, empty rows) and render N marks into a fixed canvas following a fixed slot order (reading order, snake, diagonal, bar), in item colour or constant.

parameters.item: cells | components | kxk squares of colour c | empty rows

summarise.count_to_glyph.detector: Output has a fixed shape (or size a function of N) and number of painted cells monotone in an input count; same slot prefix pattern across pairs.
summarise.count_to_glyph.primitive_sketch: N=count(select(inp)); slots=learn from train outputs (union of painted positions ordered by N); paint first N slots

summarise.ranked_bars.definition: Items (colours, objects, lines, bands) are ranked by a key (count, size, position, layering) and rendered as a list of bars/cells: one row/column per item, bar length = its count/size (or 1), aligned to a side.

parameters.key: count | height | position | occlusion order | first appearance

summarise.ranked_bars.detector: Output rows (or cols) each contain a single colour run; their colours are a permutation of input item colours sorted by a checkable key.
summarise.ranked_bars.primitive_sketch:
items=extract(inp); items.sort(key); for i,it in enumerate(items): draw bar(i, length(it), colour(it), align)
induce key/length/axis/align from train

summarise.concentric_rings.definition: An ordered list of colours (items ranked by size/count/distance/legend order) is rendered as nested concentric square rings (outer->inner), on a canvas sized by the list or inside a frame/around a seed.

parameters.items: rect outlines | colour classes | legend | scattered cells
parameters.canvas: derived square | inside frame | around seed on input

summarise.concentric_rings.detector: Output (or changed region) is a set of nested square rings, each monochrome, whose colours are a ranked list of input colours.
summarise.concentric_rings.primitive_sketch: L=ranked colour list (+ ring thickness); n=len(L); canvas=square(2n-1) or frame; for d,c in enumerate(L): paint ring at Chebyshev d

summarise.select_colour.definition: Select one object/colour by a predicate or extremum (has hole, uninterrupted line, most noise, max arm count, max growth) and output a small solid grid (1x1/2x2) of its colour.
summarise.select_colour.detector: Output is a small monochrome grid whose colour is present in input and identifies a unit that is extreme/unique by a checkable feature.

summarise.lookup_by_feature.definition: Output (whole grid or per-panel pixel) is taken from a table learned from train keyed by a discrete feature of the input (symmetry predicate, connectivity, count of distinct colours, shape class/hole pattern).
summarise.lookup_by_feature.detector: Train outputs take few distinct values (or are templates) and a single discrete feature separates them consistently.
summarise.lookup_by_feature.primitive_sketch: for f in features: table={f(x):y}; if consistent over train: return table[f(test)]

sort.rank_and_pack.definition: Items (objects, bars, cells, panels) are sorted by a key (size, length, column, count) and placed into a sequence of slots (along an edge bottom-aligned, stacked on a floor, snake order in a small canvas, nested at a corner).

parameters.slots: edge row | floor stack | 3x3 snake | nested corner

sort.rank_and_pack.detector: Output contains the same items (shape/colour preserved) at new positions whose order along the slot sequence is monotone in the key.
sort.rank_and_pack.primitive_sketch: I=sorted(items, key, order); pos=slot0; for it in I: place(it,pos); pos=next_slot(pos,it)

sort.permute_attribute_sequence.definition: Items ordered along an axis/path keep their geometry while one attribute sequence (colour, height) is reversed or cyclically shifted.
sort.permute_attribute_sequence.detector: Output has identical positions/shape multiset; the attribute sequence along the order is a reversal or rotation of the input's.
sort.permute_attribute_sequence.primitive_sketch: I=order(items); A=[attr(i) for i in I]; A2=perm(A); assign

ray.residual.definition: Tasks not covered by a generic primitive; reasons in "reasons".

reasons.e45ef808: paints only argmin/argmax height columns of a terrain; selection-by-extreme not generic ray
reasons.264363fd: template stamping at markers with arm rays to rect edges; composite
reasons.f15e1fac: rays shifted at marker rows; ray + shear composite
reasons.212895b5: diagonal rays plus staircase from sides stopping at obstacles; two motifs
reasons.ac605cbb: per-colour arm length/cap/crossing diagonal; many ad-hoc rules
reasons.3f23242b: fixed template stamp + floor line; STAMP-dominated
reasons.256b0a75: odd-L rectangle fill with band noise rays; composite
reasons.f1cefba8: notch rays that change colour inside/outside frame
reasons.a78176bb: parallel copy of diagonal offset by attachment extent
reasons.db93a21d: halo stamp + object-width downward ray; multi-layer
reasons.bae5c565: widening cone keyed by top row colours
